subject: Next steps: BrightPath integration & data-handling constraints
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Next steps: BrightPath integration & data-handling constraints

Hi Liz / Samir — thanks again for taking time earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned:

What we heard from you:
- BrightPath needs assurance that no PHI/PII is persisted beyond the request lifecycle for the clinical chat use case (you described: clinician prompts + patient context).
- You’d like model-serving to be US-resident (data plane in us-east-1) and want SOC 2 evidence.
- Procurement timeline: internal review this month; PO expected mid-September if pilot scope is acceptable.

What Redwood can offer (proposed):
- Pilot mode: input/session-level ephemeral handling (no long-term storage of raw prompts).
- Short KV cache for conversational continuity: configurable between 0–72 hours. For pilot we propose 24 hours to balance latency/cost.
- Audit logs (auth + routing) kept for 90 days; we can provide redacted request logs for QA.
- US-only data residency for the customer environment; SOC 2 summary attached.

Open items / asks from BrightPath:
1) Confirm whether any transcripts must be retained for clinical QA or legal reasons (and if so, for how long).
2) Any specific encryption/KMS requirements (bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed).
3) Procurement contact and desired contract terms (term length, renewal cadence).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik (cc) to weigh in on feasibility and suggested KV retention default for the pilot.
- If this aligns, I’ll share a one-page mutual action plan and a short pilot SOW for legal and procurement.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, data-flow-diagram.png

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick call if helpful.

—Marissa

Marissa — helpful recap, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our legal team requires that any PHI/PII used for model improvement be explicitly opt-in; for the pilot we want zero model-training persistence and minimal request retention. If you can guarantee configurable 0-retention for inputs (and confirm that no data is used to train models), that covers the immediate ask.
- For clinical QA we may need to retain a small sample of conversations for 30 days, but that’s a hard ask only if we can put automated redaction in front of it (remove PHI fields). Can Redwood do pre-storage redaction?
- We need KMS BYOK support — our security policy requires customer-managed keys for production. For the pilot, Redwood-managed keys are okay if we produce an explicit migration path to BYOK.

Procurement: I looped in procurement; they want the MAP and an estimated monthly cost for a 3-month pilot (concurrent sessions ~ 20). Procurement also asked whether Redwood can support a PO or if you require an initial MSA + SOW.

Can Karthik confirm the redaction/ephemeral options and any implications for latency?

—Liz

Subject: Re: Next steps: BrightPath integration & data-handling constraints

Liz — quick technical notes on the options Marissa proposed: 

1) Zero-persistence for model inputs: feasible. We have a deployment mode that disables request-dump persistence and prevents data from flowing into model training pipelines. This introduces no runtime latency impact.

2) Pre-storage redaction: we can implement a light-weight redaction layer that strips known PHI fields (SSNs, MRNs, clearly delimited PII) before any record is written to short-term store. Redaction is best-effort; more sophisticated de-identification (NLP-based) is possible but adds CPU overhead and ~50–120ms per request depending on model size. Pilot proposal: simple deterministic redaction for the pilot (regex+walk) to keep latency minimal.

3) KV cache retention: 0–72 hours configurable. For the clinician workflow you described, 0 means each request is stateless (no conversational context) — likely a poor UX. Our recommendation: 24 hours for the pilot; that gives session continuity within a clinician shift without long-term retention.

4) BYOK: we support KMS integration in the private deployment and Dedicated plans. For hosted pilot, we can provide Redwood-managed keys and document the migration path. Full BYOK adds ~2–4 weeks of provisioning/validation for enterprise onboarding.

Tradeoffs: shorter retention reduces storage & compliance risk but increases token re-sends from clients and may increase cost per request. Let us know what tradeoff you prefer; I can produce a short cost delta estimate for 0 vs 24 vs 72h.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: BrightPath integration & data-handling constraints

Liz / team — a couple compliance notes to capture here so legal has clarity: 

- SOC 2: attached is the one-page SOC2-summary. We can share a more detailed report under an NDA.
- Audit logs: we retain auth/routing/audit logs for 90 days by default in the hosted plan. If you need longer retention of audit records for your compliance evidence, we can discuss a custom retention window.
- Redaction guarantees: we do not offer cryptographically provable redaction. For high-assurance workflows you described, we recommend either (a) private deployment with in-customer KMS + endpoint isolation, or (b) a hybrid approach where PHI is tokenized on-prem before hitting Redwood.

If BrightPath is okay with the 24-hour KV pilot + Redwood-managed keys for the trial, we can move forward quickly. If BYOK is required for the pilot, we’ll need procurement lead time.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen | Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is useful. BrightPath can accept the following for the pilot: 

- 24-hour KV retention with deterministic pre-storage redaction for PII (we’ll provide a list of fields to redact).
- Redwood-managed keys for the 3-month pilot with a documented BYOK migration plan that must be executed before production (we expect BYOK in production).
- No model training on pilot inputs (explicitly waived).
- Audit logs retained for 90 days; BrightPath will request a monthly redacted log extract for QA.

Procurement: procurement@brightpathhealth.com is targeting a PO by Sep 20. They asked for a one-page MAP with deliverables + cost estimate for 20 concurrent sessions; can you send that today? Also we’ll need the MSA + pilot SOW templates to start redlining.

If you send the MAP and SOW today we’ll kick procurement review tomorrow.

—Liz
